text: A matrix B=[bij]_(m×m) is said to be a diagonal matrix, if: (2026 Board)

text: The order and degree of the differential equation d²y/dx² = 1 − (d³y/dx³)² is: (2026 Board)
explanation: The highest derivative is d³y/dx³ (order 3), appearing to the power 2 (degree 2) once the equation is already polynomial in derivatives.

text: For any square matrix A with real entries, a matrix B=[bij] is a diagonal matrix. Which condition matches option consistent with 65/5/3 set — For any square matrix A, if A+Aᵀ is symmetric, (A−Aᵀ): (2026 Board)

text: The order and degree of the differential equation y = (d²y/dx²)² − dy/dx is: (2026 Board)
explanation: The highest derivative present is d²y/dx² (order 2), appearing to power 2 (degree 2).

text: ∫₀¹(6x²−4x+k) dx = 0, then the value of k is: (2026 Board)
explanation: ∫₀¹(6x²−4x+k)dx = [2x³−2x²+kx]₀¹ = 2−2+k = k. Setting this to 0 gives k=0.

text: ∫√[(1+cosx)/(1−cosx)] dx is equal to: (2026 Board)

text: The order and degree of the differential equation d²y/dx² = [1−(d³y/dx³)]^(2/3) (after removing the radical) is: (2026 Board)

whyWrong: Underestimates degree after clearing the radical.

text: A cylindrical tank of radius 10 m is being filled with sand at 314 m³/h. The rate at which the height of sand increases is: (2026 Board)
explanation: V=πr²h ⇒ dV/dt=πr²(dh/dt). 314=π(100)(dh/dt) ⇒ dh/dt=314/(100π)≈1 m/h (using π≈3.14).

text: The probability that a particular item is available in three shops A, B, C is 4/5, 3/4 and 2/3 respectively. If a person visits all three shops, the probability that it is available in at least one shop is: (2026 Board)
whyWrong: This would require certainty, which is not the case.
This is P(none), not P(at least one).

text: The probability that it will rain tomorrow in cities A, B and C is 60%, 70% and 80% respectively. The probability that it will rain tomorrow in at least one of the cities is: (2026 Board)
The distance travelled by a particle in t seconds is S=72t+3t²−t³. The time taken by the particle to come to rest is: (2026 Board)
explanation: Velocity dS/dt=72+6t−3t²=0 ⇒ t²−2t−24=0 ⇒ (t−6)(t+4)=0 ⇒ t=6 s (taking the positive root).
whyWrong: This is the initial instant, not when it comes to rest.

text: y=x(dy/dx)+3√[2−(dy/dx)²]; the sum of the order and degree of this differential equation is: (2026 Board)
explanation: Isolating and squaring the radical gives an equation of order 1 with degree 2 in dy/dx, so order+degree=1+2=3.
whyWrong: The equation is well-defined after squaring.
